context.body: A messenger came to David, saying, “The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom.”.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: News of Israel’s loyalty to Absalom leads David to flee with household and servants; Ittai chooses to follow, priests bring the ark, and David returns it while leaving the outcome to God.
observations.label: David leaves Jerusalem and sends the ark back: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps David, household, servants, Ittai, Zadok, Abiathar, Levites, and the ark, Jerusalem, Kidron, wilderness road, and the ascent, hearing, fleeing, leaving concubines, testing loyalty, following, carrying, returning the ark, and yielding the outcome visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: David leaves Jerusalem and sends the ark back: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: David, household, servants, Ittai, Zadok, Abiathar, Levites, and the ark · Jerusalem, Kidron, wilderness road, and the ascent · hearing, fleeing, leaving concubines, testing loyalty, following, carrying, returning the ark, and yielding the outcome · the king departs while refusing to use the ark as security
observations.label: Relationships named in 2 Samuel 15:13–29

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 15:13–29 as its own exile, return, and rebellion David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places the king departs while refusing to use the ark as security inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
payload.title: David leaves Jerusalem and sends the ark back
